title: The 81 Theater, Lucille Achet's record shop and his Atlanta household
summary: Flowers tells him the fight world's names, including George Roby whose daughter-in-law ran a record shop by Tom Bailey's 81 Theater; Green describes Atlanta and his household of women.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You tell me about the -- I think I have -- the other part of this history in my life, fortunately, Mr. Tiger Flowers, he taught me all these -- important people's names in the fight -- in the prize fighting business at the time, and there was one gentleman named George Roby, which was Miss Lucille Achet's father-in-law. Now, Miss Lucille Achet, she used to have a record shop next door to the 81 Theater.

Now, that was Tom Bailey's theater, and it was just off five points in this city, Atlanta, Georgia, which the people there used to pride themselves on saying it was little New York City, you know, although I don't think there were

too many of them that (inaudible) would have actually visited New York City, but they would always see New York City in a lot of the films, the moving pictures that they show, you know, and, well, sure enough, after school -- I still went to school, you see, David T. Howard, and I was getting good grades, you know. But after school I would go and try to earn some money, you know, because my father was away.

And there was three ladies in my mother's -- well, it was three ladies with my mother's mother. It was two of her daughters and her and I living there on Houston in -- Hilliard Street in Atlanta, Georgia, in the Fourth Ward.
